items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: maybe some of Bacharach stuff that happened in the 60s perhaps

ctx.x: software and fake, you know like they’re loops of instruments but they repeat and repeat and repeat. And they kind of support your idea but they don’t really play your song. So I got away from that. I got away from borrowing, you know bossa nova 101 and all that stuff, and began to play the drums myself and play the bass and play the piano, play the guitar. So I would record that. I would record my drums. Record the bass. Sometimes it would be keyboard bass, sometimes I would actually pick up one of the basses.…

Junior or with Gifton Garrett — I mean Giveton Gelin — and let’s see what that sounds like just to have them both. Let’s not just mute all that work you’ve done. You’ve done all this work why should we just mute it?” So that’s so wonderful to work with an engineer who also is a musician. Do you understand? It’s not just about dials and things, this guy’s a musician too. So I’ve evolved over the course of all these decades as a writer, as a singer. And some of it is a little bit of a, I’m a little bit in a…

Somehow Scott Yanow in this book, he quoted you at the end of your entry here. And apparently you said, “I asked the jazz community, the listeners, critics and record companies to continue to support, embrace and reward originality.”
